title: 1 killed and 2 hurt in small helicopter crash off Miami, officials say | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

One person was killed and two others were injured when a small helicopter crashed Wednesday morning off Key Biscayne, Florida, theUS Coast Guardsaid, leaving the aircraft upside down with just its landing skids visible in the water near Miami.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office on Thursday identified the man killed as the helicopter’s pilot, Tomas Pendas, 63. Ryan McCoy, 52, and Ryan Ferraro, 27, were injured and airlifted to the hospital. Both have since been released.

Passengers aboard the helicopter were filming boats while heading south, the sheriff’s office said in a statement. The aircraft is part of an aerial tour and photography company owned by Pendas, according to state and Federal Aviation Administration records.

“Our hearts go out to everyone affected by this sudden and devastating event,” Petty Officer Adrian Guttierez, who works on the US Coast Guard’s search and rescue team in Miami, said in anews releaseWednesday.

The helicopter’s skids appear to have been equipped with yellow flotation devices that can inflate like a life vest to help keep it afloat if it lands or crashes in water, aerial images from the scene show.

The NTSB and FAA will investigate, both agencies confirmed, and the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office’s homicide bureau has assumed the deathinvestigation.

NTSB investigators are at the scene and will hold a briefing Thursday afternoon, the agency said.

The crash follows acollision last weekof two helicopters in Oregon that left three people dead anda crash the prior monthof a news helicopter in Los Angeles that also killed three.

The Robinson R44 helicopter involved in Wednesday’s crash took off shortly before 11 a.m. from North Perry Airport in Pembroke Pines, Florida, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.

It made several circles near the bridge to Key Biscayne, a barrier island, before turning to the south and crashing about seven minutes later.

Several agencies responded when a mayday call came from a good Samaritan around 11:30 a.m., authorities said Wednesday.

After overhearing the call, marine agents with US Customs and Border Protection working nearby recovered two injured men from the water and transported them to a harbor for medical care,CBPandthe sheriff’s Officesaid.

Separately, the sheriff’s office’s marine patrol units found a good Samaritan on a boat performing CPR on an adult male victim and took over administering first aid before bringing him to the harbor, according to the office. The victim — identified by CBP as the helicopter pilot — was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the sheriff’s office.

A safety zone was then established around the crash scene.

Thunderstorms, with lightning and light rain, along with a 9-mph wind from the east were reported around that time at the nearest weather station, Miami International Airport, about 14 miles from Key Biscayne. Gusts of 20 mph were reported closer to the site.

The Robinson R44 is a very popular small helicopter, with more than 7,800 built, according to the company. Worldwide last year, 118 were involved in crashes, including 24 fatal ones, according to theAviation Safety Networkdatabase.

There were 191 helicopter crashes last year in the US, 32 of them fatal, the safety network recorded.

CNN’s Alexandra Skores, Aaron Cooper, CNN meteorologist Mary Gilbert and Dalia Faheid contributed to this report.

This story has been updated with additional information.
